transcript:
Meeting header:
- Title: Access gating and entitlement matrix review - Meridian Logistics
- When: 2026-12-20 15:00 PST
- Duration: ~64 minutes
- Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Joanna Li (Redwood SE), Carlos Vega (Meridian Sec), Priya Menon (Meridian IT Ops), Ethan Brooks (Platform)

Summary:
Quick security/compliance deep dive focused on SSO (SAML), SCIM provisioning to Okta, and an RBAC entitlement matrix for least-privilege. Also touched on SOC 2/ISO evidence, audit log retention, and KMS/HSM workflows for keys. Customer wants clear path for hosted vs private deployment choices and data residency constraints for EU freight ops.

Topics covered:
- Current identity provider and SCIM flow
- Role design, least privilege, and entitlements matrix
- Audit logs, retention, and log forwarding (SIEM) expectations
- Encryption at rest/ in transit, KMS integration, and HSM options
- SOC 2 artifacts and ISO alignment, evidence collection
- Pilot timelines and evaluation criteria

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time, uh wanted to kick off, say quick intro from our side?
[00:14] Carlos: Yep Carlos here, head of security at Meridian, we manage the IdP — Okta - and the compliance artifacts, Priya and Ethan will cover the infra and SRE parts.
[00:27] Priya: hi all, thanks, quick ask: main concern is data residency for EU shipments, and auditability for customs data.
[00:40] Joanna: Got it, we'll cover region pinning and log export. quick note, sometimes our notes say "K-V cache" which is actually KV cache, and auto transcribers do weird stuff — apologies in advance.
[00:52] Ethan: the environment is hybrid, some nodes in our Frankfurt GCP project, some in us-west for analytics. We use Okta SCIM groups to map to internal roles.
[01:10] Samir: cool, can you run through current SCIM attributes you provision? This helps us outline the mapping to Redwood roles.
[01:21] Ethan: currently pushing okta groups with attributes: membership, title, dept, and we use a custom claim for freight-team = true. We don't sync manager or cost-center.
[01:35] Joanna: ok, for least privilege we usually recommend mapping Okta groups to minimal Redwood roles: viewer / analyst / operator / admin, then use resource-level scoping. Does Meridian have a need for resource-scoped roles?
[01:51] Carlos: yes, we need role separation by tenant and by region — EU ops cannot see US-only manifests. Also need read-only audit viewers for compliance auditors.
[02:10] Samir: that aligns. On the SAML side, are you doing SP-initiated or IdP-initiated flows?
[02:19] Priya: mostly IdP-initiated, SSO to apps, but we do have SP-initiated for some vendor tools.
[02:27] Joanna: good. For provisioning we'll map Okta groups via SCIM to Redwood roles, and then attach entitlement slices: e.g., manifest:read:europe, manifest:write:global, inference:invoke:limited.
[02:43] Ethan: question: can we attach attribute-based conditions? Like only allow certain ops during maintenance windows?
[02:50] Joanna: we support conditional RBAC via time-bound policies in our console, yes — you can set time windows and require MFA for elevated ops.
[03:05] Carlos: about audit logs — we need immutable logs for at least 3 years, and ability to forward to Splunk or BigQuery. How does Redwood expose logs?
[03:18] Samir: we stream audit events via an export API and have a log forwarder to S3/Cloud Storage, and you can pipe into your SIEM. Retention is configurable on Dedicated/Private. For hosted, default retention is 90 days but can be extended as an add-on.
[03:38] Priya: that's a key point — our compliance team will insist on 3-year retention; hosted add-on may be OK if cost is clear.
[03:48] Joanna: noted, we'll include the retention pricing in the follow up. Also automatic log signing and tamper evidence is available for Private deployments using HSM-backed signing.
[04:03] Ethan: KMS question — we use Google KMS and HashiCorp Vault for key material. Can we bring our own keys?
[04:12] Samir: yes, BYOK supported on Private and Dedicated via KMS integration; we also offer HSM with rotation policies. For hosted we support envelope encryption with customer-managed keys via external KMS connectors, though the root keys are still managed in Redwood tenancy — we'll detail the model.
[04:32] Carlos: any SOC2 evidence around key management?
[04:36] Samir: yes, SOC2 Type II includes key handling controls in our security pack. We'll share a redacted SOC2 report and a KMS control checklist.
[04:47] Priya: about least privilege, we need an entitlement matrix template — mapping Okta groups to Redwood roles and resource-level tags. Can you show an example?
[04:58] Joanna: sure, I can share a template. Generally we start with three base roles and then add scoped permissions per project/tag. Example: Logistics-Viewer -> manifest:read:region=EU, Logs-Viewer -> logs:read:project=customs.
[05:15] Ethan: how do SCIM deletes work? If someone leaves, how quickly does the role revoke?
[05:21] Joanna: SCIM de-provisioning is near real-time; we poll and apply changes within seconds to a minute depending on API rate limits. There are soft-delete grace settings.
[05:33] Carlos: concern: auditors want SAML assertion logs — can we capture raw assertions and tie them to session IDs?
[05:42] Samir: we log SAML events and session tokens; raw assertions are not stored by default for privacy, but for Private we can enable assertion archiving for X days under special agreements. We'll note compliance constraints.
[05:59] Priya: do you support SCIM mapping for nested groups? We have groups-of-groups in Okta.
[06:06] Joanna: we can flatten nested groups during provisioning or maintain group hierarchies; depends on your preference. We'll include both patterns in the template.
[06:20] Ethan: Next, encryption in transit — do you support mTLS between Redwood agents and our VPC?
[06:26] Samir: yes, for Private we can do mTLS and customer-controlled certificates; for Hosted we use TLS and mutual auth for specialized peering.
[06:38] Carlos: data residency enforcement: we need certain datasets to never leave EU. How do you enforce that?
[06:46] Joanna: we support region pinning policies and can route requests to EU-only inference capacity; we also have model variants pinned per region. For storage, we can enforce bucket-level policies in the EU.
[06:59] Priya: any caveats around fallback? If EU capacity is full will requests cross to US?
[07:06] Samir: by default we won't cross regions for pinned workloads; there is an opt-in failover policy but it must be explicitly enabled. We'll recommend a canary for traffic overflow and an SLA on cross-region failover.
[07:22] Ethan: ops question: can we get token level traces for cost attribution?
[07:27] Joanna: yes, per-token cost breakdown and request tracing are available in Console and via API. You can map tokens to project tags for chargeback.
[07:38] Carlos: auditors will ask for RBAC change history and who approved role changes. Is there an approval workflow?
[07:46] Samir: we have an audit trail and can integrate with your ticketing system for approvals, or use built-in approvals requiring two approvers for privileged role changes. All changes are logged with user and timestamp.
[08:01] Priya: any limitations on SCIM attribute sizes or special chars? Last provider we tried borked on commas in displayName.
[08:09] Joanna: we'll include quirks in the guide; we handle unicode, but there are max lengths for some attributes — we'll document exact limits.
[08:20] Ethan: competitor question — two vendors mentioned are NimbusAI and EdgeServe; we chose Redwood for runtime optimizations, but need to be sure about compliance parity.
[08:33] Samir: understood; we'll emphasize parity on SOC2/ISO and provide the controls matrix. Note: NimbusAI had different key handling, and EdgeServe had longer log retention add-on costs.
[08:47] Carlos: timeline: ideally pilot before end of quarter, production after 90 days if the pilot meets performance and audit criteria.
[08:56] Samir: good, next steps and a recap coming. Any last technical deep-dive items?
[09:05] Ethan: for pilot we'd like a benchmark of cold-start latency and end-to-end SSO flow with SCIM provisioning latency. Also a small security review runbook.
[09:17] Joanna: we can run baseline tests and provide a small playbook for the security review. We'll need Okta test tenant access for the SCIM testing.
[09:28] Priya: ok we'll provision a test Okta app and share credentials in a secure vault.
[09:34] Carlos: one more point — audit log integrity: do you support remote attestation of logs?
[09:41] Samir: for Private we've got HSM-based signing and remote attestation options; for Hosted we can provide signed log bundles as an add-on.
[09:52] Ethan: encryption key rotation policy — can we enforce quarterly rotations?
[09:57] Samir: yes, rotation policies are configurable; we recommend automated rotation with a one-week overlap window to prevent token issues.
[10:10] Joanna: I'll attach a sample entitlement matrix in the follow-up showing groups->roles->resource-slices.
[10:17] Carlos: that'll be helpful. Also need evidence for pen testing cadence.
[10:22] Samir: we publish our pen test cadence in the security pack and can share summary reports on request under NDA.
[10:30] Priya: question on service accounts — can we have machine identities with scoped keys and RBAC rather than long-lived API keys?
[10:38] Joanna: yes, short-lived certificates and service tokens with least privilege scoped roles; can be rotated automatically.
[10:45] Ethan: okay that covers most of it, maybe a few clarifying Qs later.
[10:50] Samir: great. Quick recap then next steps — we'll: 1) send SOC2/ISO summary, 2) SCIM role mapping template and quirks, 3) retention and log export pricing, 4) BYOK/KMS integration doc, and 5) schedule pilot baseline test.
[11:12] Carlos: perfect. Any blockers from our side? we'll prepare Okta test tenant and provide auditors' contact.
[11:20] Priya: yes we'll share Okta details and a list of groups by end of week.
[11:27] Samir: thanks all. I'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for pilot kickoff.

Notes / Observations (auto):
- Customer is security-forward; SOC2/ISO and 3-year audit log retention are non-negotiable. Hosted can work if add-on retention pricing is acceptable.
- Entitlement matrix will need region-scoped roles and read-only auditor roles.
- SCIM quirks: nested groups and attribute length need explicit handling.
- BYOK and HSM available on Dedicated/Private; hosted supports envelope encryption with CMK connectors.

Explicit next steps (as discussed):
1) Samir to send SOC2 Type II summary and redacted report + KMS control checklist (due 2026-12-23).
2) Joanna to share SCIM provisioning guide, sample role mapping CSV, and known attribute limits (due 2026-12-22).
3) Meridian (Ethan/Priya) to provide Okta test tenant access and list of groups (due 2026-12-24).
4) Schedule pilot baseline run week of 2026-12-27.

End of transcript.
